rows.grounds: name of the scripture, object of recognition

items.question: What identity must the fair-vowed one recognize in this teaching?
premises: The speaker addresses a fair-vowed listener directly.
The teaching is identified as the Great Liberation Tantra.
The listener is commanded to know it as such.
items.inference: The fair-vowed one must recognize this teaching as the speaker's Great Liberation Tantra.
items.plain_english: O fair-vowed one, know this as my Great Liberation Tantra.

rows.grounds: demonstrative referring to the present tantra

items.question: What supreme rank does this tantra hold among all tantras?
premises: The radiant one is supreme among luminous things.
This tantra is compared within the class of tantras.
It is declared the king of tantras.
items.inference: This tantra holds the supreme rank as king among all tantras.
items.plain_english: Thus know this as the king of tantras, radiant like the sun among luminous things.

rows.grounds: act of personally reciting or studying
act of teaching or having others recite

items.question: What spiritual attainment results from reading or teaching this tantra?
premises: A person may read this tantra.
A person may also cause others to read it.
Such engagement leads to becoming a knower of Brahman.
items.inference: By reading or teaching this tantra, a person may become a knower of Brahman.
items.plain_english: A person who has read or taught this tantra may become a knower of Brahman.

items.question: What effect does association with this tantra have on one's lineage?
premises: The statement concerns the lineage of a qualified person.
A paśu is a bound being in the practitioner grades.
The verse denies that a paśu ever arises in that lineage.
items.inference: In the lineage of such a person, a bound being never arises.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, in his lineage a bound being never arises.

rows.grounds: act of listening to the tantra

items.question: What liberation is gained by merely hearing this great tantra?
premises: A person hears this great tantra.
Karma-bondage binds beings through action.
Hearing the tantra results in release from that bondage.
items.inference: One who hears this great tantra is liberated from the bondage of karma.
items.plain_english: One who hears this great tantra is liberated from the bondage of karma.

rows.grounds: act of reverent praise or worship

items.question: What ultimate benefit does reverence to this tantra confer on people?
premises: The verse declares a salutation to the tantra.
The salutation concerns people as recipients.
It is described as giving kaivalya.
items.inference: Reverence to this tantra bestows final liberation upon people.
items.plain_english: O Supreme Goddess, salutation to it gives final liberation to people.

rows.grounds: containing or pervaded by; surface taken as given

items.question: Does any scripture surpass this tantra in containing all teachings?
premises: This tantra is endowed with all teachings.
The verse considers whether anything higher exists.
It denies the existence of anything higher anywhere.
items.inference: No scripture anywhere is higher than this tantra endowed with all teachings.
uncertainties: The form 'vitaṃ' is taken as 'endowed with' following the legacy hint; its exact derivation is unclear.
items.plain_english: This tantra, endowed with all teachings, has nothing higher than it anywhere.

items.question: What level of knowledge is attained by knowing the further half of this tantra?
premises: Someone may know the further half of this tantra.

The verse explicitly removes doubt about this claim.
items.inference: One who knows the further half of this tantra is all-knowing without doubt.
items.plain_english: Whoever knows the further half of this tantra is all-knowing; there is no doubt.

rows.grounds: events or knowledge of past, present, and future
events occurring in the three worlds

items.question: What scope of knowledge can the knower of this tantra declare?
premises: The knower is capable of telling matters of the three times.
The knower is capable of telling the account of the three worlds.

items.inference: Such a knower is capable of declaring matters of the three times and the three worlds.
items.plain_english: He is capable of telling the matters of the three times and the account of the three worlds.

rows.grounds: are worthy of or equal to

items.question: How do other teachings compare in value to the Great Liberation Tantra?
premises: The Great Liberation Tantra is the standard of comparison.
A sixteenth part represents a very small fraction.
Other teachings are said not to merit even that fraction.
items.inference: Other teachings do not merit even a sixteenth part of the Great Liberation Tantra.
uncertainties: The subject of 'arhanti' is implicit and understood as other teachings or scriptures.
items.plain_english: They do not merit even a sixteenth part of the Great Liberation Tantra.

items.question: What final liberation is attained by fully knowing this great tantra?
premises: A person may come to know this great tantra.
Brahman-liberation is the ultimate goal stated.
Knowing the tantra leads to attaining that liberation.
items.inference: One who knows this great tantra may attain liberation in Brahman.
items.plain_english: Having known this great tantra, one may attain liberation in Brahman.
